title: Data Centers
_authoring: Authored 2026-06-19 with factual, non-fabricated content (real sub-topics, real companies, real authoritative sources). Evidence grades are conservative; no synthetic DOIs. Deeper L2+ nodes flagged needs-authoring where applicable.

activations.domainDescription: The surge in electricity demand driven by AI/accelerated-compute data centers, the first sustained U.S. electricity-demand growth in roughly two decades.
activations.domainFunction: Sets the load that the rest of the energy system must serve; concentrated, fast-growing, and often clustered geographically near fiber and cheap power.
activations.whyThisNode: The hypothalamus regulates the body's overall energy demand and homeostatic set-points, mirroring how data-center load is becoming a dominant new demand the grid must balance around.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.functional_reason: Accelerated-compute hardware that drives per-rack power density and total data-center load.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.functional_reason: Hyperscale operator; major driver of new data-center electricity demand and power-purchase agreements.

companies.name: Constellation Energy
companies.functional_reason: Supplies firm, carbon-free nuclear power to data-center buyers via PPAs.

treatments.label: Integrated load-growth forecasting for data-center demand
treatments.description: Incorporate large-load (data-center) interconnection requests into utility resource planning rather than treating them as ordinary load growth; stress-test against speculative duplicate requests.
treatments.cite: IEA (2024). Electricity 2024 — Analysis and forecast to 2026 (data-centre demand section); Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (2024). United States Data Center Energy Usage Report.

citation.author: Shehabi et al. (LBNL)
citation.title: United States Data Center Energy Usage Report

steps: Separate confirmed vs speculative large-load interconnection requests (de-duplicate)
Model concentrated load clusters against local transmission capacity
Coordinate phased energization with firm-supply commitments

activations.domainDescription: Thermal management of high-density compute — air, liquid, and immersion cooling — and the freshwater consumed by evaporative cooling, increasingly contentious in drought-prone regions.
activations.domainFunction: Removes waste heat so compute can run continuously; trades electricity (chillers) against water (evaporative) and drives a shift toward liquid cooling at high rack densities.
activations.whyThisNode: The thalamus relays and regulates throughput between systems; data-center cooling is the throughput-limiting relay between compute load and sustained operation.

companies.name: Vertiv
companies.functional_reason: Liquid/air cooling and thermal-management systems for high-density data centers.

companies.name: Johnson Controls
companies.functional_reason: Chillers and building/thermal systems used in data-center cooling.

treatments.label: Shift to liquid/closed-loop cooling to cut water and energy
treatments.description: Adopt direct-to-chip or immersion liquid cooling and closed-loop/air-cooled chillers to reduce evaporative freshwater use and improve cooling efficiency at high rack densities.
treatments.cite: Uptime Institute (2023). Global Data Center Survey; U.S. DOE (2024). Data center energy efficiency resources.
steps: Audit current PUE and WUE (water usage effectiveness)
Pilot direct-to-chip liquid cooling on high-density racks
Move to closed-loop/air-cooled chillers in water-stressed sites

activations.domainDescription: The multi-year queue and transmission constraints data centers face when connecting large new loads to the grid — now a primary bottleneck on AI buildout.
activations.domainFunction: Gates whether and when new compute can be energized; drives behind-the-meter generation when the public grid can't keep up.
activations.whyThisNode: The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex gates and sequences competing demands, analogous to interconnection queues sequencing access to constrained grid capacity.

companies.name: Quanta Services
companies.functional_reason: Builds the transmission and substation infrastructure that relieves interconnection constraints.

companies.name: American Electric Power
companies.functional_reason: Transmission-heavy utility processing large data-center interconnection requests.

treatments.label: Large-load interconnection reform & flexible connections
treatments.description: Use flexible/curtailable interconnection agreements and fast-track transmission upgrades so large loads can energize sooner in exchange for accepting curtailment during peaks.
treatments.cite: FERC Order 2023 (interconnection process reform); NERC (2024). Long-Term Reliability Assessment.
steps: Offer flexible/curtailable connection agreements for large loads
Prioritize transmission upgrades at constrained nodes
Co-locate load near existing generation where possible

activations.domainDescription: Behind-the-meter and dedicated firm power for data centers — gas turbines, nuclear PPAs, restarts, SMRs, and fuel cells — when the grid can't supply fast or clean enough.
activations.domainFunction: Provides 24/7 firm power independent of interconnection timelines; central to the nuclear-restart and SMR interest driven by data centers.
activations.whyThisNode: The periaqueductal gray coordinates emergency, self-sustaining responses, mirroring on-site generation as the data center's self-supply when the grid falls short.

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.functional_reason: Gas turbines and grid equipment for on-site and utility-scale firm power.

companies.name: Bloom Energy
companies.functional_reason: Solid-oxide fuel cells deployed for on-site data-center power.

companies.name: Constellation Energy
companies.functional_reason: Nuclear PPAs and the Three Mile Island restart for data-center firm power.

treatments.label: Firm clean-power procurement (nuclear PPA / SMR / fuel cell)
treatments.description: Secure 24/7 firm power through nuclear power-purchase agreements, reactor restarts, small modular reactors (longer-dated), or on-site fuel cells, rather than relying solely on grid interconnection.
treatments.cite: U.S. DOE (2024). Pathways to Commercial Liftoff: Advanced Nuclear; IEA (2024). Electricity 2024.

citation.author: U.S. Department of Energy
citation.title: Pathways to Commercial Liftoff: Advanced Nuclear

steps: Match load profile to firm-supply options (nuclear PPA vs on-site)
Contract carbon-free firm power for baseline load
Treat SMRs as longer-dated optionality, not near-term supply

activations.domainDescription: Power Usage Effectiveness and overall efficiency — how much of a data center's power reaches compute vs overhead (cooling, conversion, distribution).
activations.domainFunction: Determines how much useful compute is delivered per kWh; gains here directly reduce demand and emissions.
activations.whyThisNode: The executive-control network optimizes resource allocation under constraint, like efficiency programs maximizing useful compute per watt.

companies.name: Eaton
companies.functional_reason: Power distribution and management equipment that reduces conversion/distribution losses.

companies.name: Vertiv
companies.functional_reason: Power and thermal systems that drive PUE improvements.

treatments.label: PUE/WUE measurement and high-voltage distribution
treatments.description: Continuously measure PUE/WUE, raise distribution voltage to cut conversion losses, and optimize airflow/thermal set-points to reduce overhead power.
treatments.cite: The Green Grid (PUE metric); LBNL (2024). United States Data Center Energy Usage Report.

citation.author: Shehabi et al. (LBNL)
citation.title: United States Data Center Energy Usage Report

steps: Instrument PUE and WUE at facility and rack level
Adopt higher-voltage DC/AC distribution to cut losses
Tune cooling set-points and airflow containment

activations.domainDescription: Uninterruptible power, battery and diesel backup, and resilience design that keep data centers running through grid disturbances.
activations.domainFunction: Bridges outages and ride-through events; increasingly battery-based and able to participate in grid services.
activations.whyThisNode: The nucleus accumbens sustains motivated activity through disruption; backup power sustains operation through grid disturbance.

companies.name: Generac
companies.functional_reason: Backup generation systems for critical facilities.

companies.name: Cummins
companies.functional_reason: Standby power generation and engines for data-center backup.

treatments.label: Battery-based UPS with grid-services participation
treatments.description: Replace or augment diesel/UPS with battery energy storage that provides ride-through and can offer demand response or frequency services back to the grid.
treatments.cite: Uptime Institute (2023). Global Data Center Survey.
steps: Assess outage exposure and required ride-through duration
Deploy battery UPS sized for resilience + grid services
Enroll capacity in demand-response/frequency programs

activations.domainDescription: Shifting or curtailing compute load in time and place to relieve grid stress — using AI workloads' partial tolerance for scheduling.
activations.domainFunction: Turns data centers from pure load into a grid asset by curtailing or relocating flexible workloads during peaks.
activations.whyThisNode: The inferior parietal lobule integrates timing and spatial context; demand flexibility is load shaped across time and location.

companies.name: Vistra
companies.functional_reason: Power supplier with flexibility/storage assets relevant to data-center load shaping.

treatments.label: Temporal/spatial workload shifting & curtailment
treatments.description: Schedule deferrable training/batch workloads to off-peak hours or lower-stress regions, and accept curtailment during grid emergencies in exchange for faster/cheaper interconnection.
steps: Classify workloads by latency tolerance
Shift deferrable compute to off-peak / low-stress regions
Contract curtailment in exchange for connection priority

activations.domainDescription: Where data centers locate — driven by power availability, water, fiber, land, tax incentives, and community/permitting acceptance.
activations.domainFunction: Determines local grid, water, and community impact; increasingly a source of friction (moratoria, rate-impact concerns).
activations.whyThisNode: The ventral pallidum gates which drives gain access to action; siting gates which projects get built where.

companies.name: Digital Realty
companies.functional_reason: Data-center REIT making large siting and power-procurement decisions.

companies.name: Equinix
companies.functional_reason: Interconnection/colocation operator siting facilities near power and fiber.

treatments.label: Power-first siting with community rate protections
treatments.description: Site near firm power and water availability, and structure tariffs so data-center load does not shift grid-upgrade costs onto residential ratepayers (a growing source of opposition).
treatments.cite: Industry siting practice; state utility-commission rate-case proceedings.
steps: Prioritize sites with firm power and water headroom
Negotiate large-load tariffs that fund their own grid upgrades
Engage communities early on rate and water impact

issues.label: Data-Center Grid Strain
issues.summary: Concentrated AI data-center load growing faster than firm supply and transmission can be added, straining regional grids and pushing operators to behind-the-meter generation.

circuits.detail: AI compute demand rising faster than the grid can serve it.
Interconnection queues and transmission limits delaying energization.
On-site/firm generation buildout compensating for grid shortfall.

issues.label: Data-Center Water & Cooling Stress
issues.summary: Evaporative cooling water use and high rack densities create local water-permit friction and force a shift to liquid/closed-loop cooling.

circuits.detail: Cooling and water demand rising with rack density.
Efficiency (PUE/WUE) becoming the constraint on siting and operation.
